swaps.why: Ramp was at 5 of 10 and Targeted disruption at 16 of 12; Go for the Throat was redundant single-target creature kill, and Farhaven Elf is ramp on a body Meren can rebuy.
A body that mills four does it every turn Meren brings it back, and it feeds the sacrifice outlets; the instant did it once.
Ramp was at 6 of 10 and Targeted disruption at 15 of 12; Infernal Grasp, Doom Blade and Murder already cover the creature half, and two-mana ramp puts Meren down a turn early.
Lands was at 37 of 38 and black at 58 pips against 24 sources; Naturalize was redundant with Krosan Grip, Reclamation Sage, Acidic Slime and Pernicious Deed.
Lands was at 37 of 38; Putrefy overlapped Assassin's Trophy, Beast Within and Infernal Grasp, and fetching two basics also helps the black source count.

review.text:
How it wins

Turns 1-3 are unchanged in shape: Stitcher's Supplier, Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Gravecrawler and Spore Frog at one mana, then Satyr Wayfinder, Rampant Growth, Animate Dead, Bloodghast, Blood Artist, Zulaport Cutthroat and Life from the Loam at two. The curve reads 1 card at zero, 6 at one, 17 at two, 22 at three, with average mana value 3.05.

Turns 4-6 Meren arrives and the deck converts. The setup cards are Stitcher's Supplier, Satyr Wayfinder, Mulch, Splinterfright, Stinkweed Imp, Golgari Grave-Troll and Life from the Loam. The cash-in cards are Meren, Victimize, Dread Return, Animate Dead, Necromancy and Moldgraf Monstrosity, plus the entry-effect bodies worth looping - Fleshbag Marauder, Plaguecrafter, Ravenous Chupacabra, Shriekmaw, Acidic Slime, Reclamation Sage, Eternal Witness and now Farhaven Elf.

Turns 7 and on: 6 cards at five mana, 2 at six, 2 at seven, 1 at eight - Living Death, Massacre Wurm, Butcher of Malakir, Moldgraf Monstrosity, Woodfall Primus.

It ends the game on drain rather than damage: Blood Artist and Zulaport Cutthroat on every death, Grave Pact, Dictate of Erebos and Butcher of Malakir emptying opposing boards, Massacre Wurm as the one card that can close three players at once.

Curve, lands and ramp

Lands is at 38 against its target of 38, and Ramp at 8 against a target of 10 - against the 5 the first review found. The three cards added (Farhaven Elf, Rampant Growth, Kodama's Reach) all cost two or three, so they come down before Meren rather than after. Ramp is still the short category that costs you something: a four-mana commander that will be killed more than once wants to be re-castable alongside a sacrifice outlet in the same turn.

Colours: black at 53 pips against 25 sources, green at 28 pips against 21. The extra Swamp and the cuts of Putrefy and Hero's Downfall moved those two toward each other from both ends. Grave Pact at {1}{B}{B}{B} and Massacre Wurm at {3}{B}{B}{B} are still the hardest casts in the deck.

One thing genuinely changed shape: instants are at 6 and creatures at 32, where the first measure read 11 instants and 30 creatures. That is a real trade. You can answer less at instant speed, but nearly all your removal now walks in on a body Meren rebuys - Ravenous Chupacabra, Shriekmaw, Fleshbag Marauder, Plaguecrafter, Acidic Slime and Reclamation Sage are each repeatable removal instead of one-shot. For this deck that is the right side of the trade; just expect to be doing your interacting on your own turn.

When the commander is answered

Unchanged, and still the strength of the deck: Animate Dead, Necromancy, Victimize, Dread Return, Living Death, Eternal Witness and Moldgraf Monstrosity all recur without Meren, and Bloodghast, Gravecrawler, Stinkweed Imp, Golgari Grave-Troll and Life from the Loam bring themselves back.

Categories

Targeted disruption is at 12 against 12 and Lands at 38 against 38 - both findings from the first review are closed.

Ramp at 8 of 10 and Card advantage at 11 of 12 are each a little short. Mass disruption at 5 of 6 is the one I would still fix: Pernicious Deed, Living Death, Massacre Wurm, Spore Frog and Tormod's Crypt is everything the deck has against a board it has fallen behind on, and nothing in the collection fills that slot - a second black sweeper would have to be a card you do not own.

Plan at 40 of 30, with theme density at 40 of 99, is the deck being itself.

The two stretch placements stand: Viscera Seer in Card advantage earns its slot as a free sacrifice outlet rather than as draw, and Spore Frog in Mass disruption answers one combat but answers it every turn once Meren is recurring it.

Bracket target 2, lowest the deck qualifies for is 2, no Game Changers, not over - leaving Demonic Tutor out is what keeps that true.

Lands that make no mana

Still one: Evolving Wilds, which sacrifices itself to fetch a basic Forest or Swamp.
